item.title: #3586711: Two CCC Scheduler permissions are never checked, and the item form saves schedules that cron cannot run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +1571/−35 · php +1371/−9 · md +196/−18 · yml +4/−8
  • Diff: b802534
  • Discussion: #3586711 · 1 contributor · 36 comments

Summary

The AI Context module declared two scheduling permissions that no code ever checked, so a role given only those could not set "Publish on" or "Unpublish on" dates. They are removed. Scheduler's own permissions for context items now do the work, and an update moves existing roles over. The item form and Content Moderation's "Change to" form now also show an error when the workflow cannot run a schedule, such as an Archived item with an "Unpublish on" date. Before, these saves succeeded and cron then failed on every run, creating a new revision each time.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Post-update ai_context_post_update_0017_use_scheduler_permissions() updates role config; no schema changes.
  • Config change: Post-update 0017 rewrites role configuration, removing the two CCC permissions and granting Scheduler's equivalents when Scheduler is installed.
  • Permission change: schedule publishing of ai context items and view scheduled ai context item removed; use Scheduler's schedule publishing of ai_context_item and view scheduled ai_context_item.

Technical details

Scheduler checks only its own schedule publishing of ai_context_item and view scheduled ai_context_item. Scheduler Content Moderation Integration (SCMI) validates scheduled transitions through constraints on publish_state and unpublish_state. Those fields are removed from the item form display, and the default states are set in AiContextItem::preSave() after validation, so SCMI never saw them. The "Change to" form saves without entity validation.

The fix adds AiContextSchedulerDefaults::getScheduledWorkflowErrors() and getStateChangeErrors(). They check the default scheduled state and the transition to it, without modifying the item. They are called from AiContextItemForm::validateForm() and ModerationFormHooks::doValidate(). Users who cannot see the date fields get the error on the moderation state, and only when the save breaks a schedule that could run before. AiContextSchedulerDefaults now takes optional content_moderation.moderation_information and scheduler.manager arguments, and the class name is an alias of the ai_context.scheduler_defaults service. These classes are @internal. Saves outside these two forms, the revert form, and existing unrunnable schedules are not checked or changed.

Post-update ai_context_post_update_0017_use_scheduler_permissions() removes the old permissions from every role. For non-admin roles it grants the matching Scheduler permission when Scheduler is installed. For admin roles it only strips the stored names. It saves only changed roles and returns a message naming them.

Upgrade

Run drush updatedb, then export and commit configuration. Importing config exported before the update restores the removed permissions and removes the Scheduler ones. Do the export before drush deploy, which runs updatedb and then imports config.

If a recipe, install profile or config export has the old names, replace them:

schedule publishing of ai context items -> schedule publishing of ai_context_item
view scheduled ai context item -> view scheduled ai_context_item

If Scheduler was not installed during the update, grant Scheduler's permissions to the roles named in the update message after installing it. A role that sets dates also needs the matching workflow transition (Publish, Restore or Archive).

item.title: #3586721: Translators can change the shared scopes of a context item from the translation form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +844/−2 · php +818/−2 · md +26
  • Diff: b208d25
  • Discussion: #3586721 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

On the translation form of an AI Context item, the settings shared by all languages are now hidden: the Context Scope controls, Priority, Specific Entities, Same as parent, Parent context and Subcontext type. Before, a translator without edit permission could change them, for example by clearing a Roles restriction or marking the item global, and the change applied to every language. This was possible when items were outside the editorial workflow. The fix also lets translations of subcontext child items be saved again. They previously failed with "Subcontext type is required when a parent context is selected."

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Users with translation permission but no edit permission could remove Roles scopes or mark an item global from the translation form when items were outside the editorial workflow.

Technical details

Core ContentTranslationHandler::entityFormSharedElements() hides untranslatable widgets on translation forms but skips details elements, and AiContextItemForm puts the scope controls, Priority, Specific Entities and Same as parent inside the context_scope details element. AiContextItemForm::form() now sets #access to FALSE on context_scope, subcontext_settings, parent and subcontext_type when sharedSettingsAreReadOnly() is TRUE. That is the case when core's content_translation translation_form form state flag is set, or when the entity is a non-default translation and isDefaultTranslationAffectedOnly() is TRUE. New items and non-translatable entities are excluded.

In the entity build step, restoreSharedSettings() writes the stored values of scope, priority, entity_items, inherit_parent_scope, parent and subcontext_type back onto the entity for those forms. A crafted POST therefore cannot change them. This also fixes the child translation save, because the hidden Subcontext type was previously submitted as empty.

On the translation form only, a warning "Fields that apply to all languages are hidden to avoid conflicting changes." is added. It links to the original language edit form only if the user has update access to the original. On the other path core already shows its own message. Editors can still change shared settings while adding a translation to items outside the editorial workflow, as in core. docs/features/multilingual.md gains a "What a translation can change" section, and functional tests were added to AiContextItemTranslationUITest.

item.title: #3586746: Site Section patterns do not match paths that have a language prefix
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +469/−26 · php +446/−25 · md +23/−1
  • Diff: 55fc7d5
  • Discussion: #3586746 · 1 contributor · 27 comments

Summary

On sites that use language URL prefixes, a Site Section pattern such as /about/* now matches the same page in every language, for example /af/about/team. Before, the prefixed page did not match, so Site Section context items were never selected there. Patterns that already include a prefix, such as /af/about/*, still work but only match that language. To limit an item to one language, add the Language scope.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Selections and subscription budget summaries now carry the config:language.negotiation cache tag, so changing URL prefixes or url.source refreshes them.

Technical details

AiContextScopeSiteSection now builds a list of request paths through a new getRequestPaths(): the path from AiContextRequestInfoResolver::getPath(), plus the same path with its language prefix removed. doGetDetectedValue(), getMatchingIndexedValues() and matchesRequestContext() all test against both, so the Relevant prefilter and the full check agree.

The prefix removal lives in the new public AiContextLanguageService::stripLanguagePrefix(). It does nothing unless language.negotiation url.source is path_prefix, so domain-based sites keep the path as is. Matching is on a whole first path segment (/afterwards is not touched), empty prefixes are skipped, and the segment is rawurldecode()d before comparison so an encoded prefix such as /op%C3%A9rations matches. The segment is split before decoding, so an encoded slash does not split it. /af becomes /. The old private extractLanguageFromPath() was replaced by findPathPrefix(), which detect() also uses, so language detection now also accepts encoded prefixes.

AiContextSelector adds the language.negotiation config as a cacheable dependency, and AiContextSubscriptionBudgetCalculator adds the config:language.negotiation tag, so changes to prefixes or url.source invalidate cached results. Kernel tests cover prefixed, encoded, unprefixed, /afterwards, domain negotiation and cache invalidation cases. docs/features/scopes.md and docs/features/multilingual.md and the Site Section form descriptions now say to write patterns without the prefix.

item.title: #3586724: Require AI 1.4.12, or document the lost generic-path context on AI 1.4.11
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +41/−50 · md +40/−49 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: d3f6d5f
  • Discussion: #3586724 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

AI Context (CCC) now requires AI 1.4.12 or later on the 1.4 branch, or AI 1.5.2 or later. On AI 1.4.11 and earlier, context that CCC pushed into automator requests and other generic chat requests did not reach OpenAI-based providers, although the debug log and the Usage tab reported the push. Sites on AI 1.4.11 or earlier must update AI before updating CCC.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal/ai constraint changes from ~1.4.11 || ^1.5.2 || ^2 to ~1.4.12 || ^1.5.2 || ^2.

Technical details

AI 1.4.11 ProviderProxy did not copy the changed system prompt back to the system role after PreGenerateResponseEvent, so context pushed on the generic path was lost while the result status and usage records still said pushed. AI 1.4.12 includes cbe279c6 on the AI 1.4.x branch (project/ai#3586825), which adds the copy-back. The commit changes the drupal/ai constraint in composer.json and updates the README and docs (docs/index.md, docs/upgrade-policy.md, docs/features/consumer_configuration.md, docs/developers/consumer_api.md, docs/developers/debugging.md, docs/developers/events.md). The "On AI 1.4.x" limits are removed, since every supported AI version now sends the ai_automator:id:{id} tag and entity_context. The temporary AiContextAutomatorIdTagSubscriber is documented as no longer needed, with its removal tracked in #3586463. The docs also note a known issue where a multi-value automator field can get earlier context blocks repeated, fixed in #3586709.

Upgrade

Update AI before CCC:

composer require drupal/ai:'~1.4.12 || ^1.5.2 || ^2'

item.title: #3586880: Add Import JSON and Export JSON to the text-only AI API Explorers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 29 files, +1572/−75 · php +1454/−59 · js +85/−16 · css +23 · yml +10
  • Diff: 363ce59
  • Discussion: #3586880 · 1 contributor · 15 comments

Summary

The Embeddings, Extractive Question Answering, Moderation, Rerank, Summarization, Text Classification, Tools and Translation explorers now have Export JSON and Import JSON, as Chat and Decision already did. Each run card gets an Export JSON button, and an Import JSON button opens a dialog where you pick a file or paste JSON. Importing fills in the form fields and, if you leave the checkbox ticked, the saved provider and model. Export works even when run history is off, which is the default. A file made for another explorer, a file with a newer version, or invalid JSON is rejected with a message saying so.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AiApiExplorerPluginBase gains opt-in JSON export/import hooks (supportsJsonExport(), exportInput(), importInput(), importFormKeys(), importIntro()) and a new ExplorerRunExport reader class.

Technical details

The shared part now lives in AiApiExplorerPluginBase. An explorer opts in by overriding supportsJsonExport() to return TRUE, which adds the import button and dialog to the intro and the export action to each run card. Subclasses shape the data with exportInput() (what leaves the file) and importInput() (which keys and types are kept; the JSON can come from anyone, so everything unknown is dropped). importFormKeys() lists fields to reset on import; Rerank adds return_all because its checkbox is derived from top_n. getEditedRunInput() now takes the FormStateInterface so an imported run wins over the ?run= query parameter, and the eight explorers pass $form_state to it.

The new final class ExplorerRunExport names formats (the _generator or _explorer plugin ID suffix is dropped, so decision_generator is ai_api_explorer_decision) and parses files in read(), which throws \InvalidArgumentException for non-object JSON, another explorer's format, a version above ExplorerRunExport::VERSION (1), or missing input. A file with no format key is treated as the bare input. The exported layout is format, version, title, input, settings.provider, and response only for successful runs. Embeddings does not export the image file ID; it writes the file's filename and mime_type under files, and import leaves the image out (archives for media explorers are tracked in #3586881). Tools import normalizes arguments and limits (only_allow or force_value).

Chat and Decision were moved onto the shared JS and PHP. A new explorer.export library (js/explorer-export.js, css/explorer-export.css) handles download and file reading. The Chat and Decision run export buttons now use the data-aie-export and data-aie-export-name attributes instead of data-aie-chat-export and data-aie-decision-export, and the old per-explorer click handlers were removed.

item.title: #3586796: Drupal 12 compatibility: add ^12 to core_version_requirement and fix removed/changed APIs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 373 files, +3097/−821 · php +2929/−706 · yml +135/−100 · neon +19/−4 · md +11/−9 · json +3/−2
  • Diff: 779d663
  • Discussion: #3586796 · 1 contributor · 26 comments

Summary

The AI module and its submodules now declare Drupal 12 compatibility, so Composer can install them on Drupal 12. The minimum supported core is raised to 11.4, so Drupal 10 and earlier Drupal 11 releases are no longer supported by this branch. Custom function call plugins and constraint definitions you maintain may need small updates to work on Drupal 12.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Requirements: core_version_requirement changed from ^10.x || ^11.x to ^11.4 || ^12 for ai and its submodules; Drupal 10 and Drupal 11 before 11.4 are no longer supported.
  • Theme change: The AI tools iframe templates (html__admin__config__ai__tools, page__admin__config__ai__tools) now use initial preprocess with ThemePreprocess instead of template_preprocess_html/template_preprocess_page.
  • API change: Function call plugins should declare execute(?object $object = NULL), and FixedValue and Choice constraints must use named options such as ['value' => 'node'] and ['choices' => [...]].

Technical details

core_version_requirement in ai.info.yml and the submodule info files is now ^11.4 || ^12, with matching changes in composer.json (drupal/key ^1.23, drush/drush ^13 || ^14, drupal/toolbar ^2.0 added) and the README dependency lines.

Code changes follow core API changes. Function call plugins (for example HelloWorld, ListColors, AutomatorPluginBase) now use execute(?object $object = NULL); the parameter is unused, and the docs say Drupal 12 requires it in the signature and that it also works on Drupal 11. Constraint options are passed with explicit names, since the diff's own test comment says Drupal 12 no longer accepts a constraint's default option without its name: 'FixedValue' => ['value' => 'node'] and 'Choice' => ['choices' => [...]]. This is applied in the docs and in ToolsExplorer, both for its limit handling and for the generated code examples. The ai_assistant_api hook_requirements() implementation moved into a AiAssistantApiRequirements class using #[Hook('runtime_requirements')] and RequirementSeverity::Warning; the procedural ai_requirements() and _ai_built_assets_requirements() were removed from ai.install, and a Drupal\ai\Hook\AiRequirements class with a runtime_requirements hook exists in the repository.

The tools iframe templates in ai_theme() switch to 'initial preprocess' pointing at Drupal\Core\Theme\ThemePreprocess:preprocessHtml and preprocessPage with an empty preprocess functions list. ai_post_update_14001() and an ai_api_explorer update no longer pass TRUE to save(). The automator_ckeditor library now lists core/jquery and core/drupal as dependencies. Tests move to the default_admin theme. CI also opts into the next major, drops the previous major jobs, and sets the Drupal 12 jobs to allow_failure. The diff returned was partial (74 of 373 files), so other changes may exist.

Upgrade

If you maintain function call plugins, update the execute() signature:

public function execute(?object $object = NULL) {

If you define FixedValue or Choice constraints on context definitions, key the options:

constraints: [
  'FixedValue' => ['value' => 'node'],
  'Choice' => ['choices' => ['article', 'page', 'blog']],
],

Sites must be on Drupal 11.4 or later.

  • Committed: November 20, 2026 (1 month later)

item.title: #3586749: Consumer settings form and post-update 0008 fail with a database error when a stored include list has a non-ASCII value (MariaDB and MySQL)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +535/−3 · php +535/−3
  • Diff: 51c2ef1
  • Discussion: #3586749 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

On MariaDB and MySQL, saving any consumer on the AI Context consumer settings form could fail with an "Illegal mix of collations" database error if another consumer's stored always_include or never_include list held a non-ASCII value such as café. The same value made post-update 0008 fail during drush updatedb. Such values can get into config through a config import, a recipe, or drush config:set. They are now ignored, and the stored value stays in configuration.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The uuid column is ASCII, and MariaDB and MySQL throw instead of matching nothing when it is compared with a non-ASCII value. AiContextConsumerForm::calculateConsumerContentDependencies() runs over every stored consumer row on each save, and _ai_context_post_update_0008_calculate_consumer_content_dependencies() did the same split. Both sorted identifiers into all-digits and everything else, then queried the everything-else group on uuid. The else branch is now elseif (Uuid::isValid($identifier)), so only numeric IDs and valid UUIDs reach the entity query. Uuid::isValid() accepts lower-case UUIDs only, so upper-case UUIDs are dropped too.

The commit also carries the matching guard for AiContextItemIdentifierResolverTrait::resolveContextItemIdentifiersToIds() from #3586741, which covers the Get Relevant tool path. The issue records that no config schema constraint was added to these sequences, because they also hold legacy numeric IDs and a constraint would make a config import with a bad value fail. New kernel tests, AiContextConsumerIncludeListNonUuidTest and AiContextIncludeListIdentifierTest, assert the value never appears in query arguments. This holds on SQLite too, which does not throw. PostgreSQL was not checked.

Contribution

  • Opened: November 18, 2026
  • Committed: November 20, 2026 (1 day later)

  • kristen pol (Itty Bitty Byte)

item.title: #3586741: Get Relevant fails with a database error when an include list has a non-ASCII value (MariaDB and MySQL)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +535/−3 · php +535/−3
  • Diff: 51c2ef1
  • Discussion: #3586741 · 1 contributor · 28 comments

Summary

The AI Context Get Relevant tool no longer fails with a database exception on MariaDB and MySQL when always_include or never_include holds a value such as a label with non-ASCII characters (for example café). Such values are now silently ignored. The same guard applies to stored consumer include lists, saving the consumer settings form, and post-update 0008, so a single bad stored value can no longer break saving any consumer or fail the database update. Include-list values must be a numeric item ID or a lower-case UUID to match anything.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

AiContextItemIdentifierResolverTrait::resolveContextItemIdentifiersToIds() sent every non-numeric identifier to an entity query on uuid. That column is ASCII, and MariaDB and MySQL raise "Illegal mix of collations" (1267) when it is compared with a non-ASCII value, while SQLite just returns no row. The trait now skips any identifier for which Drupal\Component\Uuid\Uuid::isValid() is false before it is added to the lookup list.

The identical split-and-query code in AiContextConsumerForm::calculateConsumerContentDependencies() and _ai_context_post_update_0008_calculate_consumer_content_dependencies() got the same Uuid::isValid() guard (#3586749 was closed by this change). The form runs it over every stored consumer row on each save, so one bad value in another consumer's list would previously have blocked saves.

Uuid::isValid() accepts only the lower-case 8-4-4-4-12 form. Values with a leading no-break space or zero-width space, and upper-case UUIDs, are therefore dropped before the query. Upper-case UUIDs already failed to resolve earlier, because results are keyed by the stored lower-case UUID. Dropped values stay in stored config, and post-update 0008 leaves unrecognized values unchanged. New kernel tests AiContextIncludeListIdentifierTest and AiContextConsumerIncludeListNonUuidTest assert via Database::startLog() that the value never reaches a query, so they hold on SQLite too.

Contribution

item.title: #3594905: The run snapshot does not record the --as-user default caller
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594905 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The run snapshot now records the default caller set with drush ai-eval:run --as-user, and Compare runs shows it as "Default caller". Previously a run as an anonymous visitor and a run as an administrator looked like they had identical settings. Runs recorded before this change count as having no default caller, so upgrading does not change comparisons with older runs. A re-grade keeps the caller of the run it re-grades.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalRunner adds default_caller_uid to the snapshot, cast to int when $targetConfig['default_caller_uid'] is set and NULL otherwise. RunComparability::compare() treats a missing key as NULL and, when the two values differ, adds a default_caller_uid entry to differences with a and b values. Per the added unit tests, differing callers produce a side_by_side result, and a legacy snapshot without the key compares as direct against one with NULL. ResultRegrader adds default_caller_uid to the list of snapshot keys carried over from the earlier run, and ResultsCompareController adds the "Default caller" label. No schema change.

The same commit also bundles fixes for #3594902, #3594903 and #3594904. In EvalOptimizeCommand, the failure filters (proposer prompt via formatFailures(), stored failure details, dry-run failure count) now include measured failures with a score of 0.0 and exclude questions with an error or unscored flag. In EnvelopeImporter, re-importing an envelope with the same evaluation_id now also compares target_id (source name plus dataset name) and reports a conflict if it differs, and the interval is read only from the pass rate item's score_details, so a quality score interval is no longer stored as a pass rate interval. Docs were updated accordingly.

item.title: #3594904: EEE import skips a changed dataset name as a duplicate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594904 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Re-importing an EEE envelope with the same evaluation_id but a different dataset name was reported as 'already imported' and skipped, leaving the stored row with the old test id. It is now refused as a conflict and nothing is written. An identical file is still skipped.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The imported test id (target_id) is built from source_name and source_data.dataset_name, but the measurement fingerprint omits source_data, so the fingerprint alone could not detect the change. In EnvelopeImporter, the row is now mapped with mapRow() before the duplicate lookup, and the lookup also selects target_id. A stored import is skipped only when both the fingerprint and target_id match the freshly computed row. Otherwise it is reported as conflict for evaluation_id ...: stored measurement or target differs. The fingerprint itself is unchanged and schema/*.schema.json is untouched. Tests cover a changed dataset conflicting without modifying the stored row, and an identical re-import still being skipped without a conflict. The import documentation now says a different measurement or target under the same evaluation_id is a conflict.

The same commit also bundles fixes tracked in #3594902, #3594903 and #3594905 (optimizer failure selection, default_caller_uid in run snapshots and comparability, interval handling in the importer), which are outside this issue.

item.title: #3594903: EEE import stores a quality-score interval as the pass-rate interval
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +145/−16 · php +134/−14 · md +11/−2
  • Diff: 6d37449
  • Discussion: #3594903 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Importing an EEE envelope that has no pass-rate metric no longer writes the quality score's confidence interval into the pass-rate interval columns. For example, a quality score of 4 with an interval of 3.8 to 4.2 used to be stored as pass_rate_ci_low = 3.8 and pass_rate_ci_high = 4.2. Now those columns stay empty unless the envelope reports a pass rate. Rows imported before the fix are not corrected by this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

In EnvelopeImporter::mapRow(), the interval's score_details used to come from $passRateItem ?? $primary. It now comes only from $passRateItem['score_details'] ?? []. With no pass-rate result item there is no uncertainty data, so the CI low and high values stay null. The existing pass_rate_source provenance marker still separates "not reported" from a measured zero. No schema/*.schema.json change. A new kernel test in EnvelopeImporterTest imports a 0 to 5 quality metric with an interval of 3.8 to 4.2 and asserts pass_rate is 0.0 and both CI columns are null.

The same commit also carries fixes for sibling issues #3594902, #3594904 and #3594905, which the diff shows as follows: an importer conflict check that also compares target_id, EvalOptimizeCommand failure filtering that skips errored and unscored questions, and a recorded default_caller_uid that RunComparability compares.

item.title: #3594902: The optimizer drops failures that scored 0.0
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI

item.title: #3594901: A grader that cannot be loaded drops out of scoring without a sign
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +183/−55 · php +180/−54 · md +3/−1
  • Diff: c4da6db
  • Discussion: #3594901 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Before, if a grader could not be loaded (for example its module was uninstalled, or its plugin threw in its constructor), it was silently left out of scoring. Questions and gates could then pass without that grader's check, even if it was a must-pass grader. Now a run does not start when a grader cannot be loaded, and the error names the grader and the reason. A grader that is not installed gives Could not load grader "id": it is not installed. Re-grades (the admin UI and drush ai-eval:regrade) stop with the same message.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

EvalRunner::createGraders() used to catch \Throwable, log it and drop the grader. It now still logs, then throws RunDatasetException::graderUnavailable(), a new factory on RunDatasetException (the class docblock is widened from dataset-only). That factory gives a short message for PluginNotFoundException and otherwise includes the plugin's own exception message.

For browser runs, doStartRun() checks graderManager->hasDefinition() for each configured grader before the run is created, so a missing grader means no run row and no active run. It checks only that the plugin exists, because graders are instantiated per step as the account that started the run. stepRun() now passes NULL graders to runQuestion()/runQuestionBody() (parameter type is now ?array), which load them lazily. If loading fails there, for example after the grader was removed mid-run, the question gets an error row with grader_scores empty, avg_score 0.0 and passed FALSE, and it counts toward the run's error_count. The repeated error-row arrays were extracted into questionError().

runTarget(), startRun() and regradeTarget() (via EvalRunnerInterface docblocks) can now throw RunDatasetException for this case. EvalRegradeCommand and RegradeForm catch it next to \InvalidArgumentException and show the message. No schema changes. The module docs were updated.

Upgrade

Code that calls EvalRunnerInterface::runTarget(), startRun() or regradeTarget() should also handle Drupal\ai_eval\Service\RunDatasetException, which it now throws when a grader cannot load:

catch (\InvalidArgumentException | RunDatasetException $e) {
  // Show $e->getMessage() as is.
}

item.title: #3594900: The quality gate is checked on rounded values, so 199 of 200 passes a 100% gate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +88/−39 · php +83/−36 · md +5/−3
  • Diff: e78191a
  • Discussion: #3594900 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

The AI Eval quality gate now compares the unrounded pass rate or average score with the threshold. Before, values were rounded to two decimals first, so 199 of 200 questions passing counted as 1.00 and cleared a 100% gate, and 159 of 200 (79.5%) cleared an 80% gate. Such runs now fail. The stored and displayed figures are still rounded to two decimals. Earlier runs that passed only because of rounding may have been marked as passing wrongly.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Scorer::scoreTarget() now gets its figures from a new public static Scorer::targetMetrics(). It returns valid_count, passed_count, avg_score and pass_rate, all unrounded, and skips errored and unscored questions as before. The gate goes through GateMetric::passesGate() with those values, and round(..., 2) is applied only to the returned avg_score and pass_rate.

Unrounded averages bring float error, so GateMetric::passesGate() now compares with a TOLERANCE of 1e-9. The code comment gives the example that three scores of 3.8 average to 3.7999999999999998 and must still meet a 3.8 gate. A new test covers this: 200 questions scoring 3.8 pass a 3.8 gate.

The repeated-run path in EvalOptimizeCommand::runRepeatedEval() had the same problem, because it averaged the already-rounded per-run pass_rate. It now calls Scorer::targetMetrics() on each result's question_scores, averages the unrounded values, and calls GateMetric::passesGate(). The private passesAggregatedGate() is removed. The docs were updated to describe the new behavior.

Summary

Clicking Apply on a pending prompt candidate on the AI Eval Optimize page used to always fail with an error, leaving the candidate pending and the agent prompt unchanged. Apply now saves the candidate prompt on the agent. If the agent has been deleted, Apply returns a "not found" response and the candidate stays pending.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

OptimizationController::apply() called $this->configFactory(), which ControllerBase does not provide, so the call threw and the transaction rolled back. The fix loads the ai_agent entity through entityTypeManager() and calls set('system_prompt', ...)->save() on it. Loading the entity rather than editing config directly means a deleted agent is not recreated as a config record holding only a prompt. If the ai_agents module is not installed, or the agent does not load, apply() throws NotFoundHttpException. The existing catch then rolls back the transaction, so the row stays pending. A new kernel test, OptimizationApplyTest, covers both the success path (row marked applied) and the deleted-agent path.

item.title: #3586790: Adopt Symfony AI Platform 0.12-0.14.1 changes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +516/−24 · php +508/−21 · yml +5 · json +3/−3
  • Diff: a3adad3
  • Discussion: #3586790 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

The AI module 2.x now works with Symfony AI Platform 0.14.1 instead of being pinned to 0.12. It also fixes streamed chat, which crashed with "Object of class ... could not be converted to string" whenever the model sent reasoning or tool call chunks. Models that reason before answering, such as NVIDIA ones, failed on every streamed chat. Streamed tool calls are now passed through to Drupal.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: symfony/ai-platform now requires ^0.14.1, symfony/ai-generic-platform ^0.14, and dev symfony/ai-gemini-platform ^0.14 (previously ^0.12).
  • New API: New Drupal\ai\Exception\AiStreamException (implements AiExceptionInterface); InputOutputConverter constructor takes an optional logger.

Technical details

InputOutputConverter::toStreamedChatOutput() used to cast every stream delta to string, which only works for TextDelta. The anonymous StreamedChatMessageIterator::doIterate() now maps deltas by type. TextDelta becomes a text chunk. ToolCallComplete becomes a chunk of OpenAI-shaped CreateStreamedResponseToolCall objects, one whole call each, which is the format the Drupal iterator reassembles tool calls from. Calls with an empty id (Gemini before 3.0) get a call_<index> id, and empty arguments are encoded as an empty JSON object. ToolCallStart, ToolInputDelta, the Thinking* deltas and MetadataDelta are skipped. Any other delta is skipped with a warning on the new logger.channel.ai channel, which is injected into ai.symfony.input_output_converter. A ChoiceDelta (multi-candidate stream) throws the new AiStreamException.

Tool schema building in the same class changed to match the 0.14 expectations. Each property now always carries a description and has its name key removed. The parameters array always includes required (possibly empty) and additionalProperties => FALSE. The Generic bridge now completes tool calls on any finish reason, which is why the stream fix matters more on 0.14. The issue lists follow-ups not covered here: no finish reason or token usage in streamed output, empty non-streamed token usage, Gemini text plus tool call losing the tool call, and the platform route ignoring ai.settings:request_timeout.

Upgrade

Update the Composer constraints. The requirements now resolve to:

"symfony/ai-platform": "^0.14.1",
"symfony/ai-generic-platform": "^0.14"

Run composer update drupal/ai --with-all-dependencies. Custom code that constructs InputOutputConverter directly can still do so, since the logger argument is optional.

item.title: #3586864: Translate the messages AI API Explorers write themselves for a failed run
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Version: 1.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +176/−41 · php +176/−41
  • Diff: 3b7e6c9
  • Discussion: #3586864 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

On a multilingual site, the AI API Explorers showed some failed-run messages in English even when the rest of the run card was translated, for example "The provider returned no audio." These messages the explorers write themselves are now passed through the translation system before they are stored and shown, so they can be translated like other interface text. English wording is unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Each explorer builds the message first, then throws it: $message = (string) $this->t('...'); throw new \RuntimeException($message);. The intermediate variable avoids the DrupalPractice "Exceptions should not be translated" phpcs warning. The run stores $exception->getMessage() as its error, so the stored error is in the language of the user who ran it. Covered: AiApiExplorerPluginBase ("Choose a provider and model."), Audio to Audio, Decision, Embeddings, Image Classification, Image to Image, Object Detection, Rerank, Text Classification, Text to Image, Text to Speech and ToolsExplorer (the "Access denied." fallback, the limits message, "You cannot run tools as this role."). Static methods (TextToSpeechGenerator::sample(), DecisionGenerator::parseQuestions()) use new TranslatableMarkup() instead of $this->t().

sprintf() messages became @placeholder strings. Because the exception message is plain text and escaped later when displayed, messages with placeholders are wrapped in Html::decodeEntities() so values such as a&b are not double-escaped (a DecisionGeneratorTest assertion covers this). Messages that were built from fragments became whole sentences: in EmbeddingsGenerator::toVector() the " for text N" suffix is now two separate strings per message, and in Text to Speech "Every voice failed." is translated and followed by the first error, which is already a translated sentence. The JSON parse error in parseQuestions() still comes from json_last_error_msg() and is not translated. The LogicException for developers is untouched. Tests testErrorIsTranslated were added for Audio to Audio and Tools, using locale_custom_strings_en overrides.

Upgrade

Custom explorer plugins that throw their own run errors can follow the same pattern:

// The run card shows this message to the user, so it is translated.
$message = (string) $this->t('The provider returned no audio.');
throw new \RuntimeException($message);

The Chat Explorer has a new Render Markdown checkbox on the Output tab. When it is on, assistant answers are shown as formatted HTML (headings, lists, code blocks, tables, strikethrough, and non-interactive task markers) instead of plain text. It is off by default and is saved with the chat. Copy, export and the history sent to the model keep the original raw text, and user, system and tool messages are displayed as before.

The setting is added as markdown to ChatGenerator::SETTINGS and the defaults, handled like stream and structured as an unchecked-checkbox boolean, and validated as a bool on import. buildMessage() takes a new $markdown argument and, for assistant text without schema errors, calls the new markdownBlock() instead of textBlock(). markdownBlock() converts the text and passes the HTML through Xss::filterAdmin() before it is wrapped in a div with the aie-chat__answer--markdown class. When the option is on, the chat input also gets setHostnameFilter(new HostnameFilterDto(markdownMode: TRUE)).

New CSS in the explorer stylesheet covers .aie-chat__answer--markdown (normal whitespace, pre kept, table borders, horizontal overflow).
